_note: SERVER-ONLY, like answer_key.json. Used to rank plan-review questions, to say which KINDS of behaviour his examples don't cover yet (never the cases themselves), to read his pre-mortem against known traps, and for the drift report. Never shown verbatim.

behaviours.kind_md: a run through a server pause: every scheduled request is counted, and the pause shows up in the middle and high percentiles
requests that time out or get an HTTP error are counted as errors, not left out
one slow request at the end of a short run still shows up in the top percentile
the wall clock changing during a run doesn't change measured latencies
p99.9 appears in the text report and in the JSON summary
late sends: an integer in the JSON summary and a line in the text report of a --rate run
--max-in-flight: its default, one warning the first time the cap is reached and none when it isn't, and waiting for a slot still counts from the scheduled time
--concurrency keeps its old meaning for closed-loop runs
at least one of his tests fails on Theo's original branch

traps.md: measuring latency from when the request actually went out instead of when it was scheduled, so time stuck behind a stall disappears
restarting the schedule from 'now' after falling behind, which quietly turns the open loop back into a closed loop
not counting the time a request waits for a free in-flight slot
printing the max-in-flight warning on every send, or never
leaving failed or timed-out requests out of the results, which hides the slowest requests
timing with a clock that can jump (time.time) instead of a monotonic one
rounding the percentile rank down, so the top value never reaches p99 in small runs
tests that would also pass on Theo's branch, so they don't prove the fixes
changing what --concurrency means for closed-loop runs while adding --max-in-flight
